problem: Graph Neural Network outputs leak private graph structure, enabling attackers to infer whether specific connections existed in the training graph even when observed at high precision constraints.
approach: Revisit posterior-only link-stealing attacks in strict black-box settings and propose a geometry-aware reconditioning method that reshapes intra-class distances to improve separability without harming reliability.
contribution: Demonstrates that link-stealing attacks remain effective at extremely low false-positive rates, revealing tail-risk vulnerabilities, and achieves up to 2× higher success on intra-class pairs through the proposed geometry-aware method.

problem: It is unclear how neural networks learn to perform structured operations like arithmetic and algorithmic computation when trained on sequences.
approach: Introduce the sequential group composition task where networks predict cumulative products of group elements, analyze how group structure and sequence length shape learning, and prove that two-layer networks learn one irreducible representation at a time.
contribution: Shows that two-layer networks require exponential width in sequence length but deeper architectures exploit associativity for dramatic scaling improvements—recurrent networks compose in k steps and multilayer networks in log k layers.

problem: LLM reinforcement learning suffers from rollout efficiency bottlenecks due to long-tail response length distributions with ineffective verbosity.
approach: Propose active distribution shaping to characterize and resolve long-tail distributions at fine granularity through distribution-aware trajectory sampling and adaptive redundancy allocation.
contribution: Achieves significant acceleration of up to 1.77× over state-of-the-art systems without compromising model performance by fundamentally addressing tail-induced overheads.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from high inference latency due to long visual sequences, requiring efficient on-demand utilization of visual information.
approach: Propose a training-free framework based on token embedding subspace decomposition using QR decomposition on top-K candidate embeddings to construct an orthogonal semantic basis, then measure visual impact on model predictions.
contribution: Achieves ~87% visual KV compression while maintaining over 99% of model performance through semantic impact-driven visual scheduling.

problem: RandomShuffle SGD converges faster than with-replacement SGD but requires uniformly random permutations that have high I/O complexity due to data movement across memory hierarchy.
approach: Propose a shuffling algorithm with linear I/O complexity that generates almost-uniformly random permutations using k-wise independence and matrix transposition.
contribution: Achieves the same expected theoretical convergence as RandomShuffle while reaching optimal linear I/O cost through mathematically-guaranteed k-wise independent permutations.

problem: LLM agents struggle to balance agility of direct generation against prohibitive latency of contextual integrity constraints for privacy-preserving execution.
approach: Propose PrivGate, a training-free framework that discovers a privacy manifold where models linearly encode privacy sensitivity in residual streams, using latent gating to selectively invoke explicit reasoning when high latent risk is detected.
contribution: Achieves 62.6% average relative reduction in privacy leakage with 15.9% token overhead while maintaining high performance in out-of-distribution risk identification.

problem: Enabling efficient removal of user data from trained RL agents upon deletion request while maintaining output indistinguishability from models trained without that user's data.
approach: Formulate exact unlearning in RL by constructing a ρ-TV-stable RL algorithm that supports exact unlearning with computational cost only ρ√ln T fraction of retraining from scratch.
contribution: Constructs such algorithm for tabular MDPs with regret O(H² √SAT + H³ S² A + H².⁵ S² A/ρ) and establishes lower bound Ω(H√SAT + SAH/ρ), showing near-minimax optimality.

problem: Large Language Models remain underexplored for longitudinal clinical profiles that require joint modeling of temporal dynamics and metabolic relationships.
approach: Propose STT-LLM, a structural-temporal tokenization framework that constructs biologically grounded embeddings and transforms them into LLM-compatible tokens via specialized tokenizers encoding pathway structure and temporal evolution.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements over native LLM tokenization in sequence prediction and anomaly detection on real-world longitudinal sports-doping datasets with contextual reasoning aligned to expert assessments.

problem: Outdoor LiDAR generation remains computationally intensive and lacks explicit temporal dynamics modeling, weakening spatiotemporal coherence and realism.
approach: Propose HieraScaffold, a hierarchical generation framework that disentangles and reconstructs large-scale geometry and motion using multi-resolution feature scaffolds with time-correlated distance fields and introduces neural contourlet representation to prune redundant scaffolds into minimal directional bases.
contribution: Achieves 3.3% FRD, 25.0% MMD, and 17.8% JSD improvements over strong competitors LiDMs and RangeLDM in 4D LiDAR quality and consistency.

problem: Assistive agents often complete tasks on their own rather than ceding control when important human decisions need to be made, failing to truly assist humans achieve their objectives.
approach: Propose Empower, an empowerment-maximizing method for tuning assistive language models that only requires offline examples of human-written text, providing self-supervised fine-tuning to better assist humans.
contribution: User study shows participants preferred the empowerment assistant 78% of the time with 31% higher acceptance rate, providing aligned AI agents without human feedback or verifiable rewards.

problem: Existing data attribution methods for diffusion models require access to model gradients or retraining, limiting applicability in proprietary or large-scale settings.
approach: Propose a nonparametric attribution method operating directly on data that measures influence via patch-level similarity between generated and training images, grounded in analytical form of optimal score function.
contribution: Substantially outperforms existing nonparametric baselines and achieves best attribution performance among methods that do not use target-model parameters or gradients while producing spatially interpretable attributions.

problem: Standard next-token prediction uses sparse one-hot supervision that leaves latent representation space under-constrained, allowing hidden states to drift into degenerate and anisotropic configurations.
approach: Propose Next Implicit Token Prediction (NITP) which augments discrete prediction with dense continuous supervision in representation space using shallow-layer representations as stable self-supervised targets.
contribution: Across dense and MoE models 0.5B-9B parameters, NITP achieves 5.7% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, 6.4% on C3, and 4.3% on CommonsenseQA with ~2% additional training FLOPs and no inference cost.

problem: Outcome-based RL for LLM agents fails to elicit informative feedback and internalize obtained evidence when agents must actively reason by interacting with the environment.
approach: Trace agentic behaviors into action selection and belief tracking capabilities, identify bidirectional bottleneck causing information self-locking, propose AREW that uses easy-to-obtain directional critiques to reallocate credit within trajectories.
contribution: AREW significantly mitigates information self-locking across 9 agentic tasks with up to 60-point gains in final performance.

problem: Real-world design optimization involves expensive black-box functions that generate high-dimensional auxiliary information alongside reward, but existing Bayesian Optimization methods do not leverage this.
approach: Develop a neural model predicting the objective function for unseen designs given few-shot context containing observations of auxiliary information, leveraging history of relevant previously-solved tasks.
contribution: Achieves improved few-shot prediction and faster design optimization on robotic hardware design and hyperparameter tuning, outperforming several multi-task optimization methods.

problem: Phenotypic screening produces many microscope images with biologically significant responses that are often subtle or difficult to identify, requiring effective image representations.
approach: Propose adaptations of contrastive loss functions incorporating experimental metadata as learned class vectors, introduce SPC variant where class vectors are confined to unit sphere updated only by attractive terms.
contribution: Outperforms prior methods on BBBC021, RxRx3-core, and uncurated HaCaT screens across multiple metrics with 10x smaller parameter count while maintaining improved performance.

problem: Sustainable diet implementation is hindered by inter-individual heterogeneity in aligning sustainable diet requirements with diverse personal preferences.
approach: Propose personalized sustainable diet recommendation model using constraint-aware decision-making where sustainability is incorporated through learnable constraints rather than user preferences, construct SusDiet dataset with 150k recipes.
contribution: Promotes more sustainable choices without compromising individual preference, establishing framework for aligning dietary choices with planetary health with quantitative evidence for policy-making.

problem: Symmetric multimodal-to-multimodal retrieval is critical yet underexplored, with existing methods constrained by labeled asymmetric datasets.
approach: Propose SOLAR, a two-stage self-supervised framework leveraging unlabeled web-scale image-text pairs that learns intersection mask to align intersections while preserving semantic difference.
contribution: Surpasses strongest supervised VLM by 7.08 points on a new benchmark with over 50× fewer parameters and 5× smaller embedding dimension.

problem: Knowledge distillation in language modeling shows that mixing hard and soft labels consistently yields better results, but this gain cannot be explained by closer teacher matching.
approach: Introduce Bridge-Garden Decomposition theory categorizing generation steps into Bridges (exact tokens) and Gardens (flexible tokens), develop family of hybrid supervision methods that adaptively balance hard and soft labels.
contribution: Hybrid methods outperform divergence-based and on-policy KD baselines across seven teacher-student pairs while reducing training cost by 9.7×, enabling efficient model compression.

problem: Deep learning waste segmentation methods suffer from high computational costs with large backbone networks and performance deterioration in cluttered scenes.
approach: Introduce optimal waste segmentation network utilizing spatial domain for localized structural dependencies and spectral domain for global contextual relationships, introduce auxiliary feature enhancement module.
contribution: Extensive experimentation on ZeroWaste-aug, ZeroWaste-f and SpectralWaste datasets reveals merits of the method in cluttered waste detection scenarios.

problem: Real-image editing faces a persistent trade-off between semantic editability and structural fidelity due to implicit coupling of edit progress with model scale in existing paradigms.
approach: Introduce NaviEdit, a training-free inference-time controller that decouples edit progress from model scale traversal through strict self-consistency contract, treats scale as control input reallocating step budget.
contribution: Shows positive average gains across compatible editors and flow backbones, supporting decoupling as a portable inference-time control principle.

problem: Current LLMs appear competent on benchmarks yet fundamentally misalign with what users actually seek, with existing evaluation approaches failing to capture diversity and subtlety of real expectations.
approach: Present systematic study extracting semantically rich expectations from real-world interactions, propose LENS framework enabling models to internalize user expectations for better-aligned response generation.
contribution: ExpectBench benchmark grounded in real user expectations reveals LLMs struggle to satisfy expectations, LENS consistently improves expectation satisfaction underscoring importance of explicit expectation modeling.

problem: LLMs used for zero-shot annotation and LLM-as-a-judge have reliability that hinges on how model-internalized priors interact with user-provided instructions, but this interaction is poorly understood.
approach: Investigate three dimensions: LLM familiarity with data and task definitions, extent to which additional information corrects errors (decision stickiness), and susceptibility to misaligned task definitions through experiments on toxicity detection.
contribution: Nearly two-thirds of zero-shot errors are resistant to correction with 34.8% rescue rate, Definition-Specific Familiarity shows positive association with performance (partial r=+0.41) while memorization metrics fail.

problem: Batch effects in biomedical imaging caused by technical condition alterations greatly hinder generalization of deep learning models, preventing practical deployment across multiple source and target domains.
approach: Propose CS-ARM-BN, a meta-learning batch normalization adaptation method using negative control samples as stable context for adaptation during training and inference.
contribution: Substantially improves robustness to batch size and class distribution shift on large JUMP-CP imaging dataset for Mechanism-Of-Action classification, a crucial drug discovery task.

problem: Normalizing Flows achieve promising performance on image modeling but advances in likelihood-based generative models remain limited compared to diffusion approaches.
approach: Introduce iterative TARFlow (iTARFlow) that performs autoregressive generation followed by iterative denoising inspired by diffusion methods while maintaining fully end-to-end likelihood-based objective.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on ImageNet at 64, 128, and 256 pixels, advancing frontier of Normalizing Flows as strong generative models.

problem: Deepfake detection formulated as binary classification overlooks that synthetic images are implicitly paired with real images sharing the same semantic source, and models overfit to seen fake patterns.
approach: Propose framework explicitly mining real-fake pairs using source-guided mappings or CLIP embedding nearest neighbors, introduce pair-wise discrepancy learning and discrepancy inversion with bias-only fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves superior generalization across unseen fake patterns through relationship-aware detection.

problem: MDPs with epistemic uncertainty in transition probabilities require evaluation frameworks that go beyond standard probability assumptions.
approach: Propose general theory of ambiguity-averse MDPs treating uncertain transition probabilities as random variables, extend value functions and Bellman operators, establish dynamic programming principles.
contribution: Completely characterizes law-invariant risk measures compatible with dynamic programming and delineates what is possible under the dynamic programming paradigm.

problem: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation requires long-horizon navigation and object manipulation, but most methods treat these as separate stages yielding poor navigation endpoints for manipulation.
approach: Address mismatch with 3D Interaction Chains, a unified framework coupling multi-stage navigation and manipulation planning via shared 3D feature map, stage-aligned interaction waypoints, and hierarchical policy scoring.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent gains in both task success and trajectory efficiency on simulation and real Stretch 3 robot experiments.

problem: Scaling networks in deep reinforcement learning destabilizes training and saturates performance despite architectural innovations like SimBa and BRC.
approach: Introduce ScaleMoE integrating Mixture-of-Experts modules into actor and critic, study output-level and feature-level gating schemes, progressively increase number of experts up to 64.
contribution: Across DeepMind Control Suite, MetaWorld, and HumanoidBench, progressively increasing experts significantly outperforms monolithic networks of comparable parameter counts.

problem: Estimating uncertainty for AI agents in real-world multi-turn tool-using interactions is difficult because failures occur at trajectory level from sparse critical episodes even when local generation appears confident.
approach: Introduce TRACER, a trajectory-level uncertainty metric combining content-aware surprisal with situational-awareness signals, semantic/lexical repetition, and tool-grounded coherence gaps with tail-focused risk functional.
contribution: Improves AUROC by up to 37.1% and AUARC by up to 55% over baselines in predicting task failure and enabling earlier detection of uncertainty.

problem: Sparse targets in binary logistic regression with hard labels can mislead rotation-invariant algorithms when learning noise-free soft targets.
approach: Prove that rotation-invariant algorithms like gradient descent on logistic loss incur excess risk Ω((d-1)/n) while non-rotation-invariant algorithms achieve O(s log d/n) for s-sparse targets.
contribution: Demonstrates fundamental separation between rotation-invariant and non-rotation-invariant algorithms for sparse target learning in logistic regression.

problem: Natural policy gradients remain impractical due to cost of estimating and inverting the Fisher matrix despite benefits from accounting for distribution geometry.
approach: Present Randomized Advantage Transformation (RAT) estimating Tikhonov-regularized natural policy gradients via direct backpropagation using Woodbury formula and randomized block Kaczmarz iterations.
contribution: Matches or exceeds established natural-gradient methods across continuous and visual control benchmarks while remaining simple and compatible with various architectures.

problem: Post-training lacks ground truth labels for building learning signals when improving model capabilities, especially in non-verifiable domains like healthcare.
approach: Propose Compute as Teacher (CaT) framework turning inference-time compute from parallel rollouts into supervision via reference estimation that aggregates rollouts and reward derivation using self-proposed rubrics.
contribution: On HealthBench, models match or exceed inference-time aggregation quality using 9× less test-time compute and compete with expert annotations yielding up to +30% relative improvement.

problem: RL post-training alignment for language models is costly and unstable in practice due to complicated training processes.
approach: Propose Energy-Guided Test-Time Scaling (ETS), a training-free inference method sampling from optimal RL policy via transition probability combining reference policy and energy term estimated through online Monte Carlo.
contribution: Across reasoning, coding, and science benchmarks, ETS consistently improves generation quality with provable convergence rate and practical efficiency via modern acceleration frameworks.

problem: Understanding geometry of learned distributions in diffusion models is fundamental to improvement and interpretation, but systematic tools for exploring their landscape remain limited.
approach: Introduce framework based on string method computing continuous paths between samples by evolving curves under learned score function, interpolating between pure generative transport and minimum energy paths.
contribution: For images, principal curves yield realistic morphing despite lower likelihood; for proteins, method computes transition pathways with physically plausible intermediates, establishing string method as principled tool.

problem: Precision oncology requires forecasting clinical events and trajectories but modeling sparse multi-modal clinical time series remains a critical challenge.
approach: Introduce TwinWeaver framework serializing longitudinal patient histories into text enabling unified event prediction with LLMs, build Genie Digital Twin on 93,054 patients across 20 cancer types.
contribution: Significantly reduces forecasting errors achieving median MASE of 0.87 vs 0.97 for strongest baseline, achieves average C-index 0.703 vs 0.662 for risk stratification, generalizes to out-of-distribution trials.

problem: Open Compute Project Microscaling 4-bit format (MXFP4) lags behind NVIDIA's NVFP4 in accuracy, limiting adoption for efficient LLM inference.
approach: Introduce Overflow-Aware Scaling (OAS) reducing overall errors by increasing effective dynamic range, and Macro Block Scaling (MBS) allocating higher-precision scaling at coarser granularity to preserve outliers.
contribution: OAS and MBS reduce accuracy gap between MXFP4 and NVFP4 from ~10% to below 1% on average while incurring only 6.2% GEMM overhead.

problem: Generating spatio-temporal point processes requires balancing efficient modeling of event locations, times, and counts.
approach: Propose non-autoregressive branching diffusion model starting from Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao gradient flow with drift-diffusion step and birth-death branching for count changes.
contribution: Learns reverse-time dynamics using permutation-equivariant denoiser and entropic-regularized unbalanced optimal transport, produces complete spatio-temporal event sets without autoregressive simulation.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models inherit and amplify training-data biases, both skewing coverage of predefined fairness categories and overlooking rare or minority features underrepresented in data.
approach: Introduce RAIGen, first framework for label-free rare-attribute discovery leveraging Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders and novel minority metric combining neuron activation frequency with semantic distinctiveness.
contribution: Discovers attributes beyond fixed fairness categories in Stable Diffusion, scales to SDXL, enables systematic auditing and targeted amplification of rare attributes during generation.

problem: Discrete diffusion language models require evaluation but existing metrics conflate denoiser approximation error with sampler-induced error, unlike autoregressive models.
approach: Introduce sampler-centric oracle framework replacing learned denoisers with exact Hidden Markov Model posterior, isolating sampler-induced error.
contribution: Shows few-step discrete diffusion samplers are not distributionally correct even under oracle denoiser, with transition-level mismatch vanishing only as steps approach sequence length.

problem: Reasoning models often loop, repeating the same text at low temperatures or with greedy decoding, but mechanisms causing this remain unclear.
approach: Study why looping happens with open reasoning models, introduce synthetic graph reasoning task demonstrating risk aversion and Transformer inductive biases toward temporally correlated errors.
contribution: Identifies errors in learning and Transformer biases as key causes, shows temperature reduces looping via exploration but does not fix underlying errors, discusses training-time interventions.
